summary: Cameron Bailey specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed undergraduate studies at Indiana University Bloomington under Richard F. Nance, an MA at Florida State University under Bryan J. Cuevas, and doctoral studies at the University of Oxford under Ulrike Roesler.
Cameron David Warner works in Tibetology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied under Yudru Tsomu and has held posts at Middlebury College, Dickinson College, and Aarhus University.

Cameron Foltz focuses on religious studies and Japanology. He earned an MA at Florida State University (attested 2018) under Bryan J. Cuevas and Jimmy Yu, and was attested in 2026 as a Postdoctoral Fellow at Columbia University.

Camillo Formigatti is an Indologist who studied at the University of Milan. He worked on Cambridge's Sanskrit Manuscripts Project (2011–2014), taught Sanskrit at SOAS, served as Bodleian Sanskrit Librarian (attested 2019), and was a Research Fellow at Hamburg (attested 2026).

Carel Gabriel Cobet (1813–1889) was a linguist who studied at Gymnasium Haganum and Leiden University (~1832–1836). He later taught at Leiden University in 1846 and from 1849 to 1884, where his students included Johan Hendrik Caspar Kern and Willem Caland.

Carl A. P. Ruck (born 1935) works in religious studies, history, and archaeology. He studied at the University of Michigan (~1958–1960) and Harvard University (~1960–1965), and held a post at Boston University around 1970.

Carl Bielefeldt works in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied under Shunryu Suzuki, Seizan Yanagida, and at UC Berkeley (~1974–1980). He held posts at Stanford University (~1980–2017; emeritus ~2017) and the Numata Center (attested 2017).

Carl Cappeller (1840–1925) was an Indologist and linguist. He studied in Berlin, Königsberg, Leipzig, and Jena under teachers including Franz Bopp and Albrecht Weber, and was appointed professor at the University of Jena in 1875.
Carl Christian Rafn (1795–1864) was a scholar in history, archaeology, and linguistics. He studied at the University of Copenhagen from ~1814 to 1816 and held a post there from ~1821 to 1826.

Carl Darling Buck (1866–1955) was a linguist who studied at Yale University (~1882–1889) and the University of Leipzig (~1889–1892). He served as a professor at the University of Chicago from 1892 to 1933, teaching Leonard Bloomfield and Fang-Kuei Li.

Carl Friedrich Gauss (1777–1855) studied at TU Braunschweig, the University of Göttingen (under G. C. Lichtenberg and C. G. Heyne), and the University of Helmstedt. From 1807 to 1855, he served as full professor and director of the Göttingen Observatory.
Carl Gaedicke is a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He completed his PhD at the University of Jena in 1877, where he studied under Berthold Delbrück, Eduard Sievers, and Carl Cappeller.

Carl Gustav Jung (1875–1961) was a Swiss scholar of religious studies and philosophy who earned a medical degree at the University of Basel. He held posts at the University of Zurich, ETH Zurich (1933–1942), and the University of Basel (1944).

Carl Olson specializes in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Indology, having studied under mentor John Y. Fenton. He served as the Teacher-Scholar Chair in the Humanities at Allegheny College (attested 2005–2015).

Carl Paul Caspari (1814–1892) was a scholar of religious studies and linguistics. He studied at Leipzig under H. L. Fleischer and at Berlin, and spent his career at the University of Oslo as a lektor (1847) and professor (1857).
Carl Schuster (1904–1969) was a scholar in history, archaeology, and sinology. He pursued his studies at Harvard University (~1923–1930) and the University of Vienna (~1932–1934).
Carl Shigeo Yamamoto is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Virginia under the doctoral supervision of Jeffrey Hopkins and David Germano.

Carl Siegfried (1830–1903) was a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and religious studies. Educated at Halle and Bonn, he was a Sanskrit professor at Trinity College Dublin and later held a theology professorship for Old Testament at Jena (1875–1901).

Carl W. Ernst (born 1950) is a scholar of religious studies, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Stanford and Harvard, taught at Pomona College (1981–1992), and served as professor at UNC Chapel Hill (1992–2022).

Carl Wilhelm Vollgraff (1876–1967) was a linguist and historian. After studies at Brussels, Utrecht, Göttingen, and Berlin, he served as a professor of Greek language and literature at the University of Groningen (1908–1916) and Utrecht University (1917–1946).
